newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian parties swap accusations ahead of local poll.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parties swap accusations ahead of local poll.

text.p: Albania's main political parties traded accusations on Tuesday when the ruling conservative Democratic Party accused the opposition Socialists of orchestrating a boycott of local elections later this month.
Tirana's top Socialist Musa Ulqini swiftly rejected the Democrat claim, telling reporters that his party was committed to participating in the October 20 vote.

"The strategy of the Socialist Party for solving the political and institutional crisis considers as a decisive step the participation in free and fair local polls," he said, quoting from a party resolution issued at the weekend.

Democrat secretary general Besnik Gjongecaj earlier told a news conference that the Socialists and three other opposition groups had agreed to boycott the local vote, which comes five months after a disputed general election.
The Socialists pulled out of that poll, alleging vote rigging by President Sali Berisha's Democrats. Independent observers upheld some of the Socialists' claims.
"The Socialist Party...is dishing up baseless accusations on the alleged violation of the election laws," Gjongecaj said.
He accused the opposition of trying to undermine public confidence.
"Under these circumstances the Democratic Party appeals to the Albanian electorate to embrace its alternative...We assure them of an honest and dignified elections process," he said.
All parties are presenting heavyweight candidates to win the prestigious post of Tirana mayor.
Albert Brojka last month tendered his resignation as minister for construction and tourism to run for the Democratic Party.
Agim Fagu, a former basketball star, is running for the Socialists.
